name: goddamn ransomwhere
keyCapabilities: Enterprise‑level file encryption using AES‑256‑CBC Per‑victim RSA‑2048 key management in PKCS#1 v1.5 envelopes Persistence via Windows Service creation (T1543.003) and scheduled tasks (T1053.005) Lateral movement over SMB, RDP, and VNC (T1021.x/T1076) Credential theft from browsers, Credential Manager, Wi‑Fi profiles, and signed kernel drivers for defense evasion Double‑extortion data exfiltration via Tor-based C2 channels Targeting of virtualization hosts (ESXi/Hyper‑V) and datastore encryption
description: goddamn ransomwhere (GodDamn) is a medium‑sophistication ransomware‑as‑a‑service operation targeting enterprises worldwide, especially those in critical infrastructure and high‑revenue sectors. The group encrypts files with AES‑256-CBC and an RSA‑2048 per‑victim key, combines double extortion via Tor C2 channels, and uses persistence mechanisms such as random Windows Services and scheduled tasks. Victims are pressured to pay through disposable email contacts and the qTox contact method.
goals: The group’s strategic objective is purely financial gain through high‑value extortion. By targeting sectors that operate in regulated environments—healthcare, finance, government, energy, and critical infrastructure—they maximize the perceived impact of downtime and data loss, thereby increasing ransom compliance rates. The choice of countries (US, Canada, Australia, Brazil, France, Israel, Iran, Russia) reflects a global reach and a preference for regions with large enterprise footprints and relatively robust digital infrastructures that can be breached via phishing campaigns.
